title: Netgear, EVS Team Up for Certified AV–Over–IP Live Production Workflows
body_html:
Introduction to AV-Over-IP Live Production Workflows

The collaboration between Netgear and EVS to provide certified AV-over-IP live production workflows marks a significant development in the broadcast industry. This partnership touches on critical aspects of broadcast infrastructure, including signal routing and transport, which are essential for live production environments. The use of ST 2110 or SDI fabric to connect cameras, production switchers, graphics engines, and distribution paths is a complex process that requires careful consideration of timing, redundancy, and IP routing behavior. For engineering leads, the key question is whether this development will have a measurable impact on cost, throughput, reliability, or editorial speed in live production workflows. The shift towards IP-based workflows is driven by the need for greater flexibility, scalability, and efficiency in live production. By leveraging IP protocols, broadcasters can take advantage of the flexibility and scalability of IP networks to transport audio and video signals. This, in turn, enables the creation of more complex and dynamic live productions. However, the transition to IP-based workflows also introduces new challenges, such as ensuring signal integrity, managing latency, and maintaining synchronization across the network.

Technical Breakdown of AV-Over-IP Workflows

From a technical perspective, the Netgear and EVS partnership focuses on providing a certified AV-over-IP solution that meets the requirements of live production environments. This involves ensuring that the IP network can transport high-quality audio and video signals in real-time, while also providing the necessary control and monitoring capabilities. The use of SMPTE ST 2110 transport protocols is critical in this context, as it provides a standardized framework for the transport of audio and video signals over IP networks. Additionally, the implementation of PTP/IEEE 1588 timing protocols is essential for ensuring that all devices in the network are synchronized, which is critical for maintaining lip sync and ensuring that all signals are properly aligned. The integration of NMOS discovery and control protocols is also a key aspect of the Netgear and EVS partnership. NMOS provides a standardized framework for the discovery and control of devices on an IP network, which is essential for creating a seamless and integrated live production workflow. By leveraging NMOS, broadcasters can easily discover and connect devices on the network, configure them for use in the live production workflow, and monitor their status in real-time. This enables a more efficient and flexible live production workflow, where devices can be easily added or removed as needed, and where the entire workflow can be easily monitored and controlled.

Real-World Workflow Scenarios

In a real-world live production scenario, the Netgear and EVS partnership could be used to create a highly flexible and scalable workflow. For example, a broadcaster could use the certified AV-over-IP solution to transport audio and video signals from cameras and other devices to a production switcher, where they could be mixed and edited in real-time. The use of ST 2110 transport protocols and PTP/IEEE 1588 timing protocols would ensure that all signals are properly synchronized and aligned, while the implementation of NMOS discovery and control protocols would provide a seamless and integrated workflow. The use of IP-based workflows also enables the creation of more complex and dynamic live productions. For example, a broadcaster could use the certified AV-over-IP solution to create a hybrid SDI/IP workflow, where SDI signals are converted to IP and transported over the network, while IP signals are converted to SDI and distributed to traditional SDI devices. This would enable the creation of a highly flexible and scalable workflow, where devices can be easily added or removed as needed, and where the entire workflow can be easily monitored and controlled.

Operational Implications

The Netgear and EVS partnership has significant operational implications for broadcasters. By providing a certified AV-over-IP solution, the partnership enables broadcasters to create highly flexible and scalable live production workflows, where devices can be easily added or removed as needed, and where the entire workflow can be easily monitored and controlled. This, in turn, enables the creation of more complex and dynamic live productions, where multiple signals can be transported and mixed in real-time, and where the entire workflow can be easily managed and controlled. The use of IP-based workflows also introduces new challenges, such as ensuring signal integrity, managing latency, and maintaining synchronization across the network. However, the Netgear and EVS partnership provides a comprehensive solution that addresses these challenges, while also providing a highly flexible and scalable workflow. By leveraging the certified AV-over-IP solution, broadcasters can create live productions that are more efficient, more flexible, and more scalable, while also maintaining the highest levels of signal quality and integrity.

Challenges and Limitations

While the Netgear and EVS partnership provides a comprehensive solution for live production workflows, there are still challenges and limitations that need to be addressed. One of the key challenges is ensuring that the IP network can transport high-quality audio and video signals in real-time, while also providing the necessary control and monitoring capabilities. This requires a deep understanding of the underlying network infrastructure, as well as the ability to configure and manage the network to meet the specific needs of the live production workflow. Another challenge is ensuring that the entire workflow is properly synchronized and aligned, which is critical for maintaining lip sync and ensuring that all signals are properly aligned. This requires the use of PTP/IEEE 1588 timing protocols, as well as the implementation of NMOS discovery and control protocols. Additionally, the use of IP-based workflows introduces new security challenges, such as ensuring that the network is properly secured and that all devices are properly authenticated and authorized.

Strategic Implications

The Netgear and EVS partnership has significant strategic implications for the broadcast industry. By providing a certified AV-over-IP solution, the partnership enables broadcasters to create highly flexible and scalable live production workflows, while also maintaining the highest levels of signal quality and integrity. This, in turn, enables the creation of more complex and dynamic live productions, where multiple signals can be transported and mixed in real-time, and where the entire workflow can be easily managed and controlled. The partnership also highlights the importance of IP-based workflows in the broadcast industry, and the need for broadcasters to adopt IP-based solutions in order to remain competitive. By leveraging IP-based workflows, broadcasters can create live productions that are more efficient, more flexible, and more scalable, while also maintaining the highest levels of signal quality and integrity. As the broadcast industry continues to evolve, it is likely that IP-based workflows will play an increasingly important role, and the Netgear and EVS partnership is an important step in this direction.
